I wish I wasn't so short on time right now, the problem with history is there is a lot of nuance and there is also a lot of opinion; things tend to not be simple the deeper you dig in to them but we often want simplistic answers.

So Hitler's "economic miracle" did happen but for an understanding of why is harder, it was a confluence of reasons. One of the things you need to look at is the end of WW1 and the Treaty of Versailles, Germany was given large reparations to pay and other terms which crippled them economically. So a large part of the economic miracle was Hitler discarding the conditions put in place and rebuilding Germany with government programs and rearming. An analogy could be when really fat people start exercising and then really lose weight very quickly.

There is a famous quote by Ferdinand Foch after the Treaty of Versailles: "This is not a peace. It is an armistice for twenty years". Foch realized that Germany would not remain subservient and would eventually rebuild and want revenge.

That article is good, not because it offers the truth but gives a perspective of the German / Polish relationship, it also shows how complex the relationships were in Europe since Germany was founded, which was only in the 1871.

There's a great quote I like by Francis Bacon:

"Read not to contradict and confute; nor to believe and take for granted; nor to find talk and discourse; but to weigh and consider". This is how to read history, get as many sources as possible and try to understand all angles, people that lived the events are the best as they tend to have a huge bias and with that you can see really how things really came about. History can also be depressing in many ways, you can see not only the mistakes of the past being repeated today but also how simplistic and tribal we are as a species and how we have kept doing the same thing over and over.
